# llm-agent-rag v2.0 RFC

**Date:** 2026-05-24
**Status:** DRAFT — not yet accepted
**Authors:** Generated by Plan agent during v1.x post-mortem
**Module:** `github.com/costa92/llm-agent-rag`
**Branch target:** `v2/main` (cuts after v1.9.x soak)

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The `llm-agent-rag` v1.x line froze on 2026-05-21 with v1.0.0 and accumulated thirteen tags through v1.8.0 over four days. Every minor and patch has been additive — `api/v1.snapshot.txt` has grown from the freeze baseline to **1,177 lines** without a single rename or removal. The cost of that promise is visible in the surface: `ReflectionOptions` now carries 20 fields, `Observer` carries 6 callbacks, the `rag` package exports 12 distinct error symbols, and `wrapBudgetError` appears at 6 return sites in `rag/ask.go` — a count that will roughly double when v1.9.0 (C-BudgetExpand) extends budget enforcement to `AskGlobal` and `AskDrift`.

v1.9.0 will ship as the final additive v1.x minor. After two to three patch releases of soak, `v2/main` cuts and v2.0 begins.

v2.0 will keep every existing capability and re-shape five surfaces that v1.x outgrew: ReflectionOptions becomes `ReflectionConfig` driven by functional options and named presets; `Ask` returns a typed `AskResult` whose `State` pins outcome and replaces the `wrapBudgetError` pattern; the scalar `MaxTotalTokens` knob becomes `BudgetSpec` with per-stage caps and a policy enum; a `generate.StreamModel` capability interface unlocks streaming generation without breaking `Model`; and the error taxonomy is regrouped into a documented three-tier hierarchy with the v1.x names kept as deprecation aliases.

v2.0 is not a flag day. Every v1.x exported symbol kept by v2.0 keeps its name. Symbols that v2.0 reshapes ship as `// Deprecated:` aliases for at least one v2.x minor. v1.9.x continues to receive bug fixes for six months after v2.0 GA. Streaming Provider implementations, Tree-of-Segments, and Strategy presets are explicitly out of scope for v2.0 and tracked for v2.1+.

---

## 2. v1.x State Assessment

The accretion is measurable.

| Surface | v1.0.0 freeze | v1.8.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `api/v1.snapshot.txt` total lines | (baseline) | **1,177** |
| `rag.ReflectionOptions` fields | 8 | **20** |
| `rag.Observer` callback fields | 3 (`OnImport`, `OnRetrieve`, `OnAsk`) | **6** |
| `rag` package error symbols | 4 sentinels | **6 sentinels + 1 typed struct** = 7 |
| `wrapBudgetError` return sites in `rag/ask.go` | 0 | **6** (v1.7.0+) |
| Exported `Stage*` constants | 0 | **10** (`StageAsk`, `StageReflectionDecision`, `StageGrader`, `StagePlanner`, `StageJudgeEval`, `StageAskGlobalMap`, `StageAskGlobalReduce`, `StageAskDriftPrimer`, `StageAskDriftLocal`, `StageAskDriftSynth`) |
| Cache surface (`rag` + `eval`) | none | **2 interfaces, 2 stores, 6 helpers** (v1.8.0) |

`ReflectionOptions` accretion sequence: v1.1.0 added 6 fields (chunk grading + selection + adaptive retrieval), v1.2.0 added 4 fields (active retrieval), v1.2.1 added 2 fields (parallel followups). Each minor was correctly additive; the cumulative surface is now hostile to callers using positional literals (`go vet` already advises keyed composites; the `Compatibility note: this exported struct may grow additively over time, so keyed composite literals are recommended.` doc-comment now precedes seven structs in `rag/options.go` and `rag/system.go`).

The `wrapBudgetError` pattern in `rag/ask.go` is the most legible accumulation: six return sites today, each one a manual call site that has to plumb `askStart`, `counter`, `stageUsage`, `reflection.Mode`, `rounds`, and `decisionModelCalls` through. v1.9.0 adds the same plumbing to `AskGlobal` (map and reduce legs) and `AskDrift` (primer, local, synth legs) — approximately doubling the site count to twelve before v2.0 cuts.

Observer has grown three new callbacks since freeze: `OnPlanFollowups` (v1.2.1), `OnFollowupRetrieve` (v1.2.1), `OnGenerateUsage` (v1.5.0). All three were correctly additive. Adding a seventh callback in v2.x would be done as a typed interface seam rather than a seventh field.

`generate.Model` is single-method: `Generate(ctx, req) (Response, error)`. Streaming requires a return type the interface cannot express. v1.x cannot add a second method without breaking every existing provider; v2.0's `generate.StreamModel` sibling-capability interface is the only path that respects v1.x callers.

---

## 3. v2.0 Design Pillars

### Pillar 1 — `ReflectionConfig` with functional options + presets

**Motivation.** `ReflectionOptions` is a 20-field struct where most fields have inter-field validity constraints (`AdaptiveRetrieval` requires `EnableChunkGrading`; `MaxFollowupConcurrency` is only meaningful with `ParallelFollowups`; `GraderRelevanceWeight` is only consulted under `SelectionModeBestByScore`). Today these are documented in field godoc and enforced silently in `normalizeReflectionOptions`. With 20 fields a caller cannot tell the well-formed shapes apart from the mis-shapes by reading a composite literal.

**Proposed API.** `ReflectionConfig` is an opaque struct constructed by functional options:

```go
// v2.0
type ReflectionConfig struct { /* unexported fields */ }

type ReflectionOption func(*reflectionConfigBuilder)

func NewReflectionConfig(opts ...ReflectionOption) ReflectionConfig

// Knobs (1:1 with v1.x fields, but each is now an option):
func WithMode(m ReflectionMode) ReflectionOption
func WithMaxRounds(n int) ReflectionOption
func WithMinHits(n int) ReflectionOption
func WithMinScore(s float64) ReflectionOption
func WithChunkGrading(weights GraderWeights) ReflectionOption
func WithSelectionMode(m SelectionMode) ReflectionOption
func WithAdaptiveRetrieval(threshold float64) ReflectionOption // implies grading
func WithActiveRetrieval(opts ActiveRetrievalOptions) ReflectionOption
func WithParallelFollowups(maxConcurrency int) ReflectionOption // implies active
// ... etc

// Named presets — high-traffic shapes the v1.x docs already endorse:
func PresetSelfRAG() ReflectionConfig      // chunk grading + adaptive retrieval + best-by-score
func PresetActiveRetrieval() ReflectionConfig // active retrieval + parallel followups
func PresetBudgeted(budget BudgetSpec) ReflectionConfig // rule mode + budget
```

Constraint enforcement moves into the builder: `WithAdaptiveRetrieval` records the intent to enable grading; an internal validate pass at config-finalize time returns a typed `ConfigError` listing every inter-field violation in one shot, replacing the silent normalization in v1.x.

**Migration.**

```go
// v1.x
opts := rag.AskOptions{
    Reflection: &rag.ReflectionOptions{
        Mode:                          rag.ReflectionModeHybrid,
        MaxRounds:                     3,
        EnableChunkGrading:            true,
        SelectionMode:                 rag.SelectionModeBestByScore,
        GraderRelevanceWeight:         0.6,
        GraderSupportWeight:           0.4,
        EnableActiveRetrieval:         true,
        MaxFollowupQueries:            3,
        ActiveRetrievalRelevanceFloor: 0.4,
    },
}

// v2.0
opts := rag.AskOptions{
    Reflection: rag.NewReflectionConfig(
        rag.WithMode(rag.ReflectionModeHybrid),
        rag.WithMaxRounds(3),
        rag.WithChunkGrading(rag.GraderWeights{Relevance: 0.6, Support: 0.4}),
        rag.WithSelectionMode(rag.SelectionModeBestByScore),
        rag.WithActiveRetrieval(rag.ActiveRetrievalOptions{
            MaxQueries:      3,
            RelevanceFloor:  0.4,
        }),
    ),
}
```

`ReflectionOptions` remains as a `// Deprecated:` alias type whose zero value is converted to a `ReflectionConfig` via an internal adapter; existing callers continue to compile against `*ReflectionOptions` for one v2.x minor.

### Pillar 2 — Typed `AskState` machine (replaces `wrapBudgetError`)

**Motivation.** `rag/ask.go` has 6 sites today calling `wrapBudgetError(err, askStart, counter, stageUsage, reflection.Mode, rounds, decisionModelCalls)`. The pattern exists because `Ask` returns `(Answer, error)` — partial completion has nowhere to live on the success channel, so v1.7.0 hung the partial trace off the error struct (`BudgetExceededError.PartialDiagnostics`). v1.9.0 extends the pattern to `AskGlobal` and `AskDrift`, doubling the site count.

**Proposed API.** v2.0 returns a typed result whose `State` field pins outcome:

```go
// v2.0
type AskState int

const (
    AskStateUnknown AskState = iota
    AskStateFinal              // Answer fully assembled, no abort.
    AskStatePartial            // Aborted before final round; Answer is best-effort partial.
    AskStateAborted            // Aborted by policy (budget, validation, etc.); Answer is zero value.
    AskStateCancelled          // ctx.Done(). Answer is zero value.
)

type AskResult struct {
    State       AskState
    Answer      Answer        // Zero value when State == AskStateAborted | AskStateCancelled.
    Diagnostics Diagnostics   // Always populated, even on Partial/Aborted.
    AbortReason error         // Non-nil when State != AskStateFinal. Sentinel-matchable.
}

func (s *System) Ask(ctx context.Context, question string, opts AskOptions) (*AskResult, error)
```

`error` is reserved for genuine system failures (nil store, nil model, ctx cancelled by parent). Budget abort, validation abort, and partial-round abort all flow through `AskResult.State` + `AbortReason`. Callers stop pattern-matching `errors.As(err, &budgetErr)` and start switching on `result.State`.

The six (soon twelve) `wrapBudgetError` sites collapse to a single internal helper that fills `AskResult.Diagnostics` and sets `State` + `AbortReason` — the pattern moves from "wrap an error six times" to "compute a result once".

**Migration.**

```go
// v1.x
ans, err := sys.Ask(ctx, q, opts)
var be *rag.BudgetExceededError
if errors.As(err, &be) {
    // recover partial via be.PartialDiagnostics
    log.Printf("budget exceeded at %s; partial rounds=%d", be.Stage, len(be.PartialDiagnostics.Reflection.RoundDetails))
    return be.PartialDiagnostics, nil
}
if err != nil { return nil, err }

// v2.0
res, err := sys.Ask(ctx, q, opts)
if err != nil { return nil, err } // genuine system failure only
switch res.State {
case rag.AskStateFinal:
    return res.Answer, nil
case rag.AskStatePartial, rag.AskStateAborted:
    log.Printf("ask aborted (%v): %v", res.State, res.AbortReason)
    return res.Answer, nil // Answer is partial or zero-value
case rag.AskStateCancelled:
    return zero, ctx.Err()
}
```

`Ask` (v1.x signature) ships as a `// Deprecated:` shim that calls the new `Ask` and converts `AskStateAborted`-with-budget-reason back into the v1.7.0 `*BudgetExceededError` form for one v2.x minor.

### Pillar 3 — `BudgetSpec` (replaces scalar `MaxTotalTokens`)

**Motivation.** `AskOptions.MaxTotalTokens int` is a single cumulative cap with one policy (abort on overage). v1.7.0 documents two gaps: budget enforcement is Ask-only; the only policy is abort. v1.9.0 closes the first gap. The second gap — operators who want a warn-only mode, or per-stage caps so reflection cannot consume the planner's tokens — has no clean additive surface within v1.x.

**Proposed API.**

```go
// v2.0
type BudgetSpec struct {
    // Total caps cumulative TotalTokens across all stages. Zero is unlimited.
    Total int
    // PerStage caps cumulative TotalTokens per named stage. Missing stage = inherit Total.
    // Keys match the rag.Stage* constants: "ask", "reflection_decision", "grader", etc.
    PerStage map[string]int
    // OnExceeded selects the policy when any (Total or PerStage) cap is exceeded.
    OnExceeded BudgetPolicy
}

type BudgetPolicy int

const (
    PolicyAbort    BudgetPolicy = iota // Default: terminate Ask, State=AskStateAborted.
    PolicyWarn                         // Fire Observer.OnBudgetWarning, continue.
    PolicyTruncate                     // Skip non-critical stages (grader, planner) once exceeded; continue answer leg.
)
```

`AskOptions.Budget BudgetSpec` replaces `AskOptions.MaxTotalTokens int`. The zero `BudgetSpec` is unlimited / abort — byte-identical to v1.7.0 zero-value semantics.

`PolicyTruncate` is the new capability v1.x cannot express. It enables a "graceful degradation" mode where a long-running Ask exhausts its grader and planner budget mid-reflection but still produces a final answer with the rounds it already had.

**Migration.**

```go
// v1.x
opts := rag.AskOptions{ MaxTotalTokens: 1000 }

// v2.0
opts := rag.AskOptions{
    Budget: rag.BudgetSpec{
        Total:      1000,
        OnExceeded: rag.PolicyAbort,
    },
}

// v2.0 new capability — per-stage caps:
opts := rag.AskOptions{
    Budget: rag.BudgetSpec{
        Total: 1000,
        PerStage: map[string]int{
            rag.StageGrader:  200,
            rag.StagePlanner: 100,
        },
        OnExceeded: rag.PolicyTruncate,
    },
}
```

`AskOptions.MaxTotalTokens int` remains as a `// Deprecated:` field for one v2.x minor; when both `Budget.Total == 0` and `MaxTotalTokens != 0`, the latter is promoted to `BudgetSpec{Total: MaxTotalTokens, OnExceeded: PolicyAbort}` by an internal adapter.

### Pillar 4 — Streaming generation seam (`generate.StreamModel`)

**Motivation.** `generate.Model` is single-method `Generate(ctx, req) (Response, error)`. Streaming generation requires either yielding tokens incrementally (channel/iterator) or accepting a callback. Neither shape fits the `(Response, error)` signature, and v1.x's additive-only promise forbids adding a method to `Model` — every implementing provider would break.

FLARE-style look-ahead generation and Tree-of-Segments retrieval (both v2.1+ candidates per the design notes) both need access to partial output during generation. Without a streaming seam the door stays shut.

**Proposed API.** Sibling-capability interface — type-assert pattern, identical in shape to v1.0.3's `embed.BatchEmbedder` and v1.0.6's `store.LexicalSearcher`:

```go
// v2.0 — in generate/model.go
type Token struct {
    Text         string
    LogProb      float64    // 0 when provider does not report.
    UsageDelta   Usage      // Per-token usage delta (provider-reported, may be zero).
    Done         bool       // True on the terminal sentinel token.
}

// StreamModel is an optional sibling-capability over Model. A Model
// implementation that also satisfies StreamModel can be consumed by
// streaming-aware callers; plain Model implementations are unchanged.
//
// The receive channel closes naturally when the stream ends. On error,
// the error is delivered on a separate channel returned alongside;
// implementations must close both channels before returning.
type StreamModel interface {
    Model // every StreamModel is also a Model (non-streaming fallback)
    GenerateStream(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Token, <-chan error)
}
```

The `Model` super-interface is preserved verbatim. Every v1.x provider continues to compile. New providers opt into streaming by adding the second method. The `rag.System` answer paths use a type-assertion check:

```go
// in rag/ask.go (v2.0)
if sm, ok := s.model.(generate.StreamModel); ok && s.streamingEnabled {
    // streaming code path; falls back to sm.Generate when streaming inappropriate
}
// existing non-streaming path otherwise — unchanged.
```

**Migration.** No migration is required for existing callers — `generate.Model` is unchanged. New streaming-aware code opts in by implementing or type-asserting `StreamModel`.

v2.0 ships **the interface only**. Streaming Provider implementations (OpenAI, Anthropic, llmagent) ship in subsequent Provider releases — see Section 6 (Out of Scope).

### Pillar 5 — Unified error taxonomy

**Motivation.** The `rag` package today exports 6 sentinel errors and 1 typed struct, organized by feature accretion rather than by category:

- `ErrEmptyQuery` (v0.1.x — validation)
- `ErrModelRequired` (v0.1.x — wiring)
- `ErrImporterRequired` (v0.1.x — wiring)
- `ErrRetrieverRequired` (v0.1.x — wiring)
- `ErrSourceRequired` (v0.1.x — validation)
- `ErrCommunitySummarizerRequired` (v0.5.0 — wiring)
- `ErrTokenBudgetExceeded` + `BudgetExceededError` (v1.7.0 — policy)

There is no documented type hierarchy and no shared interface a caller can switch on. The `eval` and `obs` packages have their own. Categorizing every new error becomes ad-hoc.

**Proposed API.** Three documented tiers, with the v1.x names retained as aliases:

```go
// v2.0 — Tier 1: sentinel errors (compare with errors.Is)
var (
    ErrInvalidArgument = errors.New("rag: invalid argument")        // umbrella
    ErrConfigRequired  = errors.New("rag: required configuration missing") // umbrella
    ErrAborted         = errors.New("rag: operation aborted by policy")    // umbrella

    // Concrete sentinels (wrap an umbrella sentinel via Unwrap):
    ErrEmptyQuery                  // wraps ErrInvalidArgument
    ErrSourceRequired              // wraps ErrInvalidArgument
    ErrModelRequired               // wraps ErrConfigRequired
    ErrImporterRequired            // wraps ErrConfigRequired
    ErrRetrieverRequired           // wraps ErrConfigRequired
    ErrCommunitySummarizerRequired // wraps ErrConfigRequired
    ErrTokenBudgetExceeded         // wraps ErrAborted
)

// Tier 2: typed wrappers (compare with errors.As, carry context)
type BudgetError struct {
    Stage  string
    Used   int
    Budget int
    Spec   BudgetSpec        // The full spec, not just the scalar.
    // PartialDiagnostics moves to AskResult.Diagnostics — see Pillar 2.
}
func (e *BudgetError) Error() string
func (e *BudgetError) Unwrap() error // returns ErrTokenBudgetExceeded

type ValidationError struct {
    Field   string
    Message string
}
func (e *ValidationError) Error() string
func (e *ValidationError) Unwrap() error // returns ErrInvalidArgument

type ConfigError struct {
    Violations []ConfigViolation // From ReflectionConfig builder (Pillar 1).
}
func (e *ConfigError) Error() string
func (e *ConfigError) Unwrap() error // returns ErrConfigRequired

// Tier 3: external-cause wrappers (network, model, store) — out of scope for v2.0.
```

Callers gain a documented switch:

```go
// v2.0
res, err := sys.Ask(ctx, q, opts)
switch {
case errors.Is(err, rag.ErrInvalidArgument): // user input
case errors.Is(err, rag.ErrConfigRequired):  // wiring
case errors.Is(err, rag.ErrAborted):         // policy
case err != nil:                              // unexpected
}
```

**Migration.** Every v1.x error name is preserved verbatim. `BudgetExceededError` is renamed to `BudgetError` and keeps the v1.x name as a `// Deprecated:` type alias. `PartialDiagnostics` moves from the error to `AskResult.Diagnostics` — the alias provides a `Compatibility() Diagnostics` helper that pulls from the parent `AskResult` when the error was produced by the shim.

|---|---|---|
| `rag.ReflectionOptions` (struct, 20 fields) | renamed → `ReflectionConfig`; v1.x name kept as deprecated type alias | Field-by-field functional-option mapping; one v2.x minor of overlap. |
| `rag.AskOptions.MaxTotalTokens int` | replaced by `AskOptions.Budget BudgetSpec`; field kept deprecated | Auto-promotion adapter for one v2.x minor. |
| `rag.BudgetExceededError` (struct) | renamed → `BudgetError`; v1.x name kept as deprecated alias | `PartialDiagnostics` moves to `AskResult`; `.Compatibility()` helper bridges. |

## 5. Timeline + Migration Strategy

```
2026-05-24    v1.8.0 (current — C-Cache + C-MarkdownExport)
2026-MM-DD    v1.9.0  (C-BudgetExpand — final additive minor)
2026-MM-DD    v1.9.1  (soak patch)
2026-MM-DD    v1.9.2  (soak patch, optional)
2026-MM-DD    v2/main branches from v1.9.x
2026-MM-DD    v2.0-RC1  (Pillars 1-5 wired; deprecation shims live)
2026-MM-DD    v2.0-RC2  (feedback-driven; timing flexible)
2026-MM-DD    v2.0 GA
              v1.9.x continues bug-fix-only for 6 months after v2.0 GA
2026-MM-DD    v2.1+  (streaming Providers, Tree-of-Segments, Strategy presets)
```

**Migration commitments to v1.x callers:**

1. Every v1.x exported symbol that v2.0 keeps verbatim retains its name and signature.
2. Every v1.x symbol that v2.0 reshapes ships a `// Deprecated:` bridge for at least one v2.x minor (i.e. through v2.1).
3. `go vet` and the `deprecation` analyzer surface every deprecation site so callers can ratchet down at their own pace.
4. The `api/v1.snapshot.txt` test stays green for one v2.x minor — the v1 snapshot continues to assert that the v1-named surface compiles, even when the underlying types are aliases.
5. v1.9.x receives bug fixes only for 6 months post-v2.0 GA. New features land on `v2/main`.

**For the SDK author:**

- `v2/main` cuts from `main@<v1.9.x soak tag>`; the first commit on `v2/main` is the module path bump (`module github.com/costa92/llm-agent-rag/v2`).
- The `contract` package's pinned-symbol list re-baselines against the v2.0 surface at v2.0 GA; cross-repo consumers update their `require` at their own cadence.

---

## 6. Out of Scope for v2.0

v2.0 is the surface-reshape release. The following are explicitly **not** v2.0 deliverables:

- **Streaming Provider implementations.** v2.0 ships the `generate.StreamModel` interface and the `rag.System` type-assertion check, but no Provider implementation. OpenAI, Anthropic, and `llmagent`-adapter streaming support land in subsequent provider releases on their own cadence.
- **Tree-of-Segments retrieval.** Depends on streaming generation to detect mid-answer information gaps. v2.1+ candidate.
- **FLARE / lookahead generation.** Same dependency. v2.1+ candidate.
- **Strategy presets** (`SelfRAGStrategy`, `ActiveStrategy`, `BudgetedStrategy` as full pipelines, not just reflection presets). Discussed in v1.5+ planning; full implementation is v2.1+. v2.0 ships `PresetSelfRAG()` / `PresetActiveRetrieval()` / `PresetBudgeted()` as `ReflectionConfig` builders only.
- **`Diagnostics` reshape.** The deeply nested `Diagnostics` struct (Reflection/Global/Drift/GraphTrace) accretion is acknowledged but reshaping it touches every observability consumer downstream. Deferred to a separate v2.x consideration.
- **`Observer` → interface conversion.** Surveyed and rejected for v2.0 (see Manifest). May revisit in v2.x.
- **Error tier 3** (external-cause wrappers for network/model/store failures). v2.0 ships tiers 1 + 2 only.
- **`eval` package reshape.** The eval package has grown 21 source files since v1.3.0 but its public surface is well-organized; v2.0 leaves it alone.
- **`postgres` driver rev.** The pgx/pgvector dependency line is unchanged in v2.0.

---

## 7. Open Questions

These resolve before v2.0 GA. Each is a discuss-phase candidate for the user.

1. **Should `AskResult.State == AskStatePartial` ever be returned with a usable `Answer`?**
   The current v1.7.0 behavior returns the zero-value `Answer` on budget abort. `AskStatePartial` opens the door to "you got 2 of 3 reflection rounds; here is the best round so far". The trade-off: callers that today rely on `Answer.Text == ""` as the abort signal need a new check. Proposal: yes, but gated on a new `AskOptions.ReturnPartialOnAbort bool` (default false → byte-identical to v1.7.0 abort semantics).

2. **Does `BudgetSpec.PerStage` keys validate against the known `Stage*` constants, or are arbitrary keys accepted?**
   Arbitrary keys are flexible (custom Graders may emit custom stage tags) but typos go undetected. Proposal: validate against the 10 known constants in the builder, return a `ConfigError`; callers can opt out via `BudgetSpec{PerStageStrict: false}`.

3. **`generate.StreamModel.GenerateStream` return signature: `<-chan Token, <-chan error)` vs single `<-chan StreamEvent` where `StreamEvent` is a sum type?**
   Two channels match Go convention (errgroup-style) and let providers signal terminal error after token close; a single channel is simpler but error semantics are less obvious. Proposal: two channels; revisit if iterator pattern (Go 1.23+ `range func`) becomes idiomatic.

4. **Should `ReflectionConfig` builder errors abort `NewReflectionConfig` (panic-or-zero-config) or surface as `(ReflectionConfig, error)`?**
   Functional-options libraries split on this. Proposal: `NewReflectionConfig(...) ReflectionConfig` never errors; finalize-time validation runs lazily on first use inside `Ask`, returning a `*ConfigError` via the normal error path. Avoids constructor-time panics; cost is that bad config is detected later.

5. **`v2.0-RC1` content scope: do all five pillars land in RC1, or do they ratchet across RC1/RC2/RC3?**
   Argument for one-shot: deprecation shims need to settle together so callers can test the full migration. Argument for ratcheting: smaller RCs are easier to review and revert. Proposal: Pillars 1, 2, 5 in RC1; Pillars 3, 4 in RC2; full integration soak in RC3.
